question: Kushal and Brijesh together invested ₹63,300 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹17,600, Brijesh's share was ₹2,200. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Kushal's Profit = Total Profit − Brijesh's Profit = ₹17,600 − ₹2,200 = ₹15,400

Profit Ratio (Kushal : Brijesh) = 15,400 : 2,200 = 7 : 1

Since the investment time period is the same, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio = 7 : 1

Difference in investment = (7 − 1) ÷ (7 + 1) × Total Investment

Difference = 6/8 × 63,300 = ₹47,475

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47,475.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹63,300

Total profit = ₹17,600

Brijesh's share in profit = ₹2,200

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Capital × Time

When time is constant, Capital Ratio = Profit Ratio.

 Total Profit = ₹17,600
 
• 
 
• 
 
 Kushal: ₹15,400
 
 Brijesh: ₹2,200
 Profit Ratio = 7 : 1
 Investment Ratio (Same Time) = 7 : 1
 Total Investment = ₹63,300 (8 parts)
 Difference (6 parts) = ₹47,475

**Calculations:**

⇒ Kushal's Profit = Total Profit − Brijesh's Profit

⇒ Kushal's Profit = 17,600 − 2,200 = 15,400

⇒ Profit Ratio (Kushal : Brijesh) = 15,400 : 2,200 = 154 : 22 = 7 : 1

⇒ Since both invested for a year (time is constant), investment ratio is equal to the profit ratio.

⇒ Investment Ratio (Kushal : Brijesh) = 7 : 1

⇒ Total Investment = 7 parts + 1 part = 8 parts

⇒ 8 parts = 63,300

⇒ 1 part = 63,300 ÷ 8 = 7,912.5

⇒ Difference in their investments = 7 parts − 1 part = 6 parts

⇒ Difference = 6 × 7,912.5 = 47,475

**∴ The correct answer is ₹47,475.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When the capital of all the partners is invested for the same duration of time, the profit is distributed exactly in the ratio of their invested capital.

Compound Partnership

When the capital of the partners is invested for different time periods, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of their capital and respective time periods (Profit Ratio = Capital ₁ × Time ₁ : Capital ₂ × Time ₂).

Sleeping Partner

A partner who only invests capital but does not actively participate in the business operations. They receive a share of the profit purely based on their investment without any operational salary.
